notes: Migrated from hardcoded definitions in debugger.py / daa_fa_engine.py.

led_codes.blinking_blue: Bluetooth pairing mode, ready for app
led_codes.blinking_yellow: Soft reset in progress or weak connection
led_codes.solid_red: Critical error, hardware or connection failure

1.name: PoE Input Stage
1.desc: Verify PoE power delivery and 5V system rail

2.name: Miami SoC Core
2.desc: SoC core voltages - unit won't boot without these

3.name: DDR4 Memory
3.desc: DDR4 power - boot hangs at DDR training if failed

4.name: Shared / Analog
4.desc: Shared 1.8V = single point of failure for WiFi + Ethernet

6.name: WiFi / Waikiki / PCIe
6.desc: Waikiki radio and PCIe link supplies

V_POE_POWER_RAIL.name: PoE Power Rail
V_POE_POWER_RAIL.fail_action: Check PoE injector, cable, bridge rectifier. 0V=open input. <42.5V=injector weak or cable too long.

POE_POWER_UBOOT.name: PoE Power at U-Boot
POE_POWER_UBOOT.loc: Read from PoE injector or bench PSU display

V_TP1205_POE_5V.name: POE 5V Rail
V_TP1205_POE_5V.fail_action: 0V=MPM3690 not switching (check ENABLE, class resistor). <4.75V=overloaded/cap degradation. >5.25V=feedback failure.

V_TP579_VDD_CX.name: VDD_CX (Miami Core)
V_TP579_VDD_CX.fail_action: MOST CRITICAL. 0V=Buck1/SPBM failure. Measure R to GND (>5ohm OK, <1ohm=Miami die short).

V_TP27_VDD_SOC_CX.name: VDD_SOC_CX
V_TP27_VDD_SOC_CX.fail_action: SoC core. If differs from TP579=trace/filter issue. Check ferrite bead.

V_TP29_VDD_SOC_MX.name: VDD_SOC_MX
V_TP29_VDD_SOC_MX.fail_action: Memory bus domain. Missing while VDD_CX OK=separate LDO failed.

V_TP578_VDD1V95_PMU.name: VDD1V95_PMU
V_TP578_VDD1V95_PMU.fail_action: PMU supply. Missing=upstream 5V/3.3V issue. Low=PMU LDO drooping.

V_TP574_VDD_DDR.name: VDD_DDR (1.2V)
V_TP574_VDD_DDR.fail_action: DDR4 core. 0V=Buck3 fail. Low=BGA short. Ripple>30mV=cap degradation. BGA crack RPN=162.

V_TP576_VDD_LDO_2P5_VPP.name: VDD_LDO_2P5_VPP
V_TP576_VDD_LDO_2P5_VPP.fail_action: DDR4 word-line pump. Must come AFTER VDD_DDR. Missing=LDO/sequencing issue.

V_TP503_VDD1P8_NAPA.name: VDD1.8 NAPA (Shared)
V_TP503_VDD1P8_NAPA.fail_action: SHARED RAIL: Waikiki analog + Napa PHY I/O. Missing=WiFi AND Ethernet dead. Check Buck 2.

V_TP28_VAA_0P8.name: VAA_0P8
V_TP28_VAA_0P8.fail_action: 0.8V analog ref. Missing=LDO failed. Check enable and input.

V_TP36_VAA_1P2.name: VAA_1P2
V_TP36_VAA_1P2.fail_action: 1.2V PLL analog reference. Out-of-spec may cause PLL jitter or clock drift. Monitor only — does not indicate board-level failure on its own.

V_TP504_VDD1P05_NAPA.name: VDD1.05 NAPA Core
V_TP504_VDD1P05_NAPA.fail_action: Napa core. 0V=Buck5 fail. Needs both 1.05V AND 1.8V(TP503). Check SGMII/MDIO/magnetics.

V_TP573_DVDD3P3.name: DVDD3.3 (Waikiki)
V_TP573_DVDD3P3.fail_action: Waikiki main digital. 0V=Buck6 fail. Present but no WiFi=check PCIe (PERST_N, clock).

V_TP535_DVDD5.name: DVDD5 (Waikiki 5V)
V_TP535_DVDD5.fail_action: 5V to Waikiki. Missing=5V bus distribution issue. Low=excess load/cap degradation.

V_TP589_DVDD3P3_BZT.name: DVDD3.3_BZT
V_TP589_DVDD3P3_BZT.fail_action: Should track TP573. Different=isolation component open/shorted.

V_TP34_VDD_PCIE_0P925.name: VDD_PCIE_0P925
V_TP34_VDD_PCIE_0P925.fail_action: PCIe SerDes analog supply. Out-of-spec may degrade PCIe link margin. Monitor only — WiFi failure more likely caused by DVDD3.3 or PERST_N.

V_TP31_VDD_1V8_PX3.name: VDD_1V8_PX3
V_TP31_VDD_1V8_PX3.fail_action: 1.8V PX3. Missing while other 1.8V OK=local LDO issue.

V_TP569_VDD_XPA.name: VDD_XPA (5G PA)
V_TP569_VDD_XPA.fail_action: HIGHEST RAIL. Feeds SKY85500 FEMs (8.4W peak). 0V=Buck8 fail. Low=FEM PA short.

V_TP577_AVDD3P3_2G.name: AVDD3.3_2G (2.4G IPA)
V_TP577_AVDD3P3_2G.fail_action: 2.4G internal PA. 0V=Buck7 fail. Present but no 2.4G=Miami IPA or SAW filter damaged.

V_TP55_STBY.name: STBY_VDD3.3
V_TP55_STBY.fail_action: Standby 3.3V always-on. Missing=early power failure before SPBM.

V_TP590_LED.name: LED_5V_3V3
V_TP590_LED.fail_action: LED driver supply. 0V=no LED. Present but dark=I2C bus or KTD2027B failure.

V_TP56_USB_A.name: USB-C Orient (A)
V_TP56_USB_A.fail_action: USB-C CC detection pin. Out-of-spec indicates FUSB15201MX orientation detect issue. Monitor only — does not affect core board function.

V_TP56_USB_B.name: USB-C Orient (B)
V_TP56_USB_B.fail_action: USB-C CC alternate orientation. Out-of-spec indicates CC resistor network issue. Monitor only — does not affect core board function.
V_TP56_USB_B.loc: TP56 — same pad as step 24, measure with cable flipped

POE_POWER_QSDK.name: PoE Power QSDK
POE_POWER_QSDK.fail_action: <3W=subsystems not running. >12.9W=abnormal, thermal camera for short.
POE_POWER_QSDK.loc: Read from PoE injector or bench PSU display

PoE Input.schematic_path: RJ45 → PoE Magnetics → Bridge Rectifier → MPM3690GQJ-Z → 5V/6A System Bus
PoE Input.description: Fully integrated PoE PD controller. Converts 37-57V DC from Ethernet cable to 5V system bus at up to 6A (30W). 802.3at Class 4 classification. 300KHz fixed-frequency switching. PGOOD signal feeds SPBM for sequencing.

failure_modes.0V output: Input diode short or FET failure. Check Vin at bridge output.
failure_modes.Low output: Cap degradation or excessive load. Measure 5V under load.
failure_modes.Oscillation: Feedback loop instability. Scope 5V rail for ripple >50mV pk-pk.
failure_modes.Overtemp shutdown: Poor thermal pad solder. Thermal image MPM3690 pad area.
failure_modes.Classification fail: Wrong classification resistor value. Verify 24.9K for Class 4.

component_diagnostics.check: DMM continuity: pins 4,5 (V+) and pins 7,8 (V-) to bridge rectifier input. Visually inspect for bent pins, corrosion, water residue.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Replace RJ45 jack. Check magnetics for open winding (DCR ~1Ω each pair).

component_diagnostics.location: Adjacent to RJ45, between magnetics and MPM3690
component_diagnostics.check: With PoE applied, measure DC voltage at bridge output (cathode side). Diode test in-circuit (one direction conducts ~0.4V, reverse open).
component_diagnostics.expected: 37–57V DC at bridge output. Diode drop 0.3–0.7V forward, OL reverse.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Shorted diode → 0V at TP1207. Replace failed diode. Common cause: ESD/lightning surge.

component_diagnostics.location: Center-left, large QFN package near TP1205
component_diagnostics.check: 1) ENABLE pin (post-classification) should be HIGH (~3V). 2) Touch test top of IC — should be warm but not >80°C. 3) Scope SW pin: 300kHz square wave when running.
component_diagnostics.expected: EN ≈ 3V, SW pin = 300kHz switching, package <70°C steady-state
component_diagnostics.if_fail: EN low → classification rejected by PSE (check classification resistor next). No SW switching → IC dead, replace MPM3690. Hot >85°C → thermal pad solder void, reflow or rework.

component_diagnostics.check: With board powered OFF and PoE disconnected, measure resistance from RCLASS pin to GND.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Wrong value → PSE classifies incorrectly, may not deliver full 30W. Replace with 24.9K 1% 0402.

component_diagnostics.location: Largest inductor near MPM3690, between SW pin and TP1205
component_diagnostics.check: DCR check (board off): should be <50mΩ. Visual: no cracks, no scorching, solder joints intact.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Open inductor → 0V at TP1205. Cracked core → low/oscillating output. Replace with same part (saturation current ≥8A).

component_diagnostics.check: Visual: cracks, lifted pads, solder bridges. Scope 5V at TP1205 AC-coupled, 20MHz BW: ripple should be <50mV pk-pk.
component_diagnostics.expected: No visible damage, ripple <50mV pk-pk at full load
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Cracked ceramic = capacitance loss → high ripple, possible oscillation. Replace all 4 caps as a set.

component_diagnostics.location: Trace from MPM3690 PGOOD pin to SPBM input
component_diagnostics.check: With 5V rail healthy at TP1205, PGOOD pin should go HIGH (~3.3V) ~10ms after 5V settles.
component_diagnostics.expected: PGOOD = HIGH (3.0–3.3V) when 5V rail is in regulation
component_diagnostics.if_fail: PGOOD stuck LOW → SPBM blocks downstream sequencing → no Buck converters start, even if 5V is OK. Check pull-up resistor and trace continuity to SPBM.

TP1207.schematic_path: RJ45 Center Taps (pins 4,5=V+; 7,8=V-) → Bridge Rectifier → TP1207
TP1207.description: Measures the raw PoE voltage after the bridge rectifier, before the DC/DC conversion. This is the 37-57V DC rail from the Goldfinch PSU via Ethernet cable. 0V here means no PoE power is reaching the board at all.

failure_modes.0V: No PoE power. Check cable, injector, RJ45 connector, magnetics center taps.
failure_modes.<42.5V: Weak injector or long cable run (>100m). Check cable resistance.
failure_modes.>57V: Non-compliant PSU. Risk of overvoltage damage.

component_diagnostics.check: Measure injector output at the cable head (pins 4,5 vs 7,8) with no load. Then with the unit connected. Try a known-good cable <30m.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Bad injector or cable. Swap to a known-good Class 4 PSE before suspecting the board.

component_diagnostics.component: RJ45 jack pins and PCB solder joints
component_diagnostics.check: Inspect jack under microscope: bent center-tap pins (4,5,7,8), cold solder, water/corrosion. Wiggle test under load — voltage should stay rock-steady.
component_diagnostics.expected: All pins straight, solder fillets clean, no corrosion
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Re-solder pins, or replace jack if pins are damaged. Corrosion → field exposure issue, log as IP66 seal failure.

component_diagnostics.location: Inline between RJ45 and bridge rectifier
component_diagnostics.check: DCR each winding (board off): both pairs ~1Ω. Inter-winding isolation should be >100MΩ.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Open winding → 0V at TP1207. Shorted to data pairs → fries the magnetics. Replace module.

component_diagnostics.location: Between magnetics and MPM3690 input cap
component_diagnostics.check: Diode test in-circuit, board off. Forward 0.3–0.7V each, reverse OL. Look for cracked package after a surge event.
component_diagnostics.expected: All 4 diodes show forward drop and reverse open
component_diagnostics.if_fail: One shorted diode = full bridge collapse → 0V at TP1207. Replace failed diode (check the others — surges often kill multiple).

component_diagnostics.location: Largest cap at MPM3690 VIN pin (typically 1uF/100V or 2.2uF/100V)
component_diagnostics.check: Visual inspect for bulging, cracks, lifted pads. Out-of-circuit ESR / capacitance check if available.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Open cap → input ringing, possible MPM3690 damage. Replace with same rating (≥80V).

TP1205.schematic_path: MPM3690GQJ-Z SW pin → L (inductor) → TP1205 → 5V bus → All Buck converters
TP1205.description: Main 5V system rail. Output of the PoE PD converter. Feeds ALL downstream buck converters (Buck 1-8). This is the single most important power rail — if this is dead, nothing works.

failure_modes.0V: MPM3690 not switching. Check ENABLE pin (should be HIGH from classification). Check input voltage at TP1207.
failure_modes.<4.75V: Overloaded (downstream short) or output cap degradation. Measure current draw. Check for shorted buck converter.
failure_modes.>5.25V: Feedback resistor divider failure. Check FB pin network.

component_diagnostics.check: Resistance from TP1205 to GND, board OFF. Healthy = ~10kΩ falling slowly (cap charge). Short = <1Ω.
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Hard short → DO NOT power up. A downstream Buck IC (1-8) is shorted. Lift the ferrite beads one at a time to isolate which Buck is shorted.

component_diagnostics.check: With PoE applied, measure EN pin voltage. Should be HIGH (~3V) after PSE classification (~50ms after plug-in).
component_diagnostics.if_fail: EN stuck LOW → classification failed (check 24.9K class resistor) or MPM3690 internal damage. EN HIGH but no SW = MPM3690 dead.

component_diagnostics.check: Scope SW pin (10x probe, AC-couple). Should see clean 300kHz square wave with sharp edges.
component_diagnostics.expected: 300 kHz ±10%, 0V to ~Vin square wave, rise time <50ns
component_diagnostics.if_fail: No switching → IC failure, replace MPM3690. Slow edges → bootstrap cap (CBOOT) failed, replace 100nF cap on BST pin.

component_diagnostics.location: Largest inductor between SW pin and TP1205
component_diagnostics.check: Board OFF: DCR <50mΩ. Visual: cracked ferrite, scorching, lifted solder. Under load: not >Curie temp (~120°C).
component_diagnostics.expected: DCR 10–40mΩ, no cracks, runs <100°C at full load
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Open → 0V at TP1205. Saturated/cracked → high ripple, MPM3690 may shut down on overcurrent. Replace.

component_diagnostics.check: Scope ripple at TP1205 under full load. Visual: cracked dielectrics. Pull and measure cap value if suspicious.
component_diagnostics.expected: Ripple <50mV pk-pk at 30W load, all caps within 20% of nominal
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Cracked ceramic = ESR jumps, ripple >100mV, MPM3690 may oscillate. Replace all 4 as a set (X5R/X7R, ≥10V rated).

component_diagnostics.location: Two 0402 resistors near MPM3690 FB pin
component_diagnostics.check: Board OFF: measure RFB1 (top) and RFB2 (bottom). Expected ratio sets 5.0V output.
component_diagnostics.expected: Per datasheet for 5V output (typically RFB1≈40.2K, RFB2≈10K — verify against schematic)
component_diagnostics.if_fail: Wrong/lifted resistor → output too high (>5.25V can damage downstream) or too low. Replace bad resistor.

component_diagnostics.check: If TP1205 reads <4.75V, measure each Buck input ferrite bead to GND. The shorted one will read <1Ω.
component_diagnostics.expected: All Buck inputs read >100Ω to GND (board off)
component_diagnostics.if_fail: The shorted Buck is your culprit — it's pulling the 5V rail down. Common causes: overcurrent stress, BGA solder short under SoC.

TP579.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 1 (0.9V/8A, 700KHz) → TP579 → Miami IPQ5332 VCC_CX pins
TP579.description: MOST CRITICAL RAIL. 0.9V core supply for Miami IPQ5332 SoC. Powers ARM cores, DSP, and all digital logic. 8A max at 700KHz switching. Without this rail, the SoC is completely dead — no boot, no LED, no UART.

failure_modes.0V: Buck 1 or SPBM failure. Measure resistance VCC_CX to GND: >5Ω = open (converter dead), <1Ω = Miami die short.
failure_modes.<0.88V: Buck 1 drooping under load. Check inductor, output caps. Possible Miami excess current draw.
failure_modes.>0.99V: Feedback network failure. Overvoltage risk to SoC.

TP27.schematic_path: TP579 (VDD_CX) → Ferrite Bead → TP27 → Miami IPQ5332 VDD_SOC_CX pins
TP27.description: Filtered version of VDD_CX. Passes through a ferrite bead for noise filtering before reaching the SoC core pins. Should track TP579 closely. A significant delta between TP579 and TP27 indicates a filter component issue.

failure_modes.Differs from TP579: Ferrite bead open or high-resistance. Check continuity between TP579 and TP27.
failure_modes.Both 0V: Upstream Buck 1 failure — debug at TP579 first.

TP29.schematic_path: Internal LDO (from VCC_CX domain) → TP29 → Miami IPQ5332 VDD_SOC_MX pins
TP29.description: Separate voltage domain for Miami's memory bus interface. Generated by an internal LDO inside the SoC from the VCC_CX domain. If VDD_CX is present but VDD_SOC_MX is missing, the internal LDO has failed.

failure_modes.0V while VDD_CX OK: Miami internal LDO failure. SoC may need replacement.
failure_modes.0V with VDD_CX also 0V: Upstream power issue — debug Buck 1 first.
failure_modes.Low voltage: Excessive memory bus current. Check DDR4 signals.

TP578.schematic_path: 5V Bus → LDO → TP578 → Miami IPQ5332 PMU input pins
TP578.ic: PMU LDO (feeds Miami internal power management)
TP578.description: 1.95V supply for Miami's internal Power Management Unit. The PMU generates several internal LDO outputs for the SoC. If this rail is missing, Miami's internal regulators cannot function even if VCC_CX is present.

failure_modes.0V: Upstream 5V/3.3V bus issue or PMU LDO failure. Check 5V rail first.
failure_modes.Low (<1.9V): LDO drooping — check input voltage and load current.

TP574.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 3 (1.2V/2A, 1MHz) → TP574 → DDR4 Nanya NT5AD512M16C4 VDD pins
TP574.description: 1.2V core supply for DDR4 SDRAM. Must be stable before Miami releases DDR reset. Ripple >30mV indicates cap degradation. DDR4 BGA solder joint cracking is the #3 risk item (RPN=162) in failure analysis.

failure_modes.0V: Buck 3 converter failure. Check enable signal from SPBM.
failure_modes.<1.14V: Possible BGA short pulling rail down. Measure resistance to GND.
failure_modes.Ripple >30mV: Output cap degradation. Replace ceramic caps on 1.2V rail.
failure_modes.DDR training fail: Rail present but noisy. Scope AC-coupled, 20MHz BW. Also check BGA solder joints (X-ray if available).

TP576.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 4 (2.5V/0.6A, 1MHz) → TP576 → DDR4 VPP pins
TP576.description: 2.5V word-line pump voltage for DDR4. Required for DDR4 activation. MUST come up AFTER VDD_DDR (1.2V) is stable — power sequencing is critical. If VPP is missing while VDD_DDR is present, the DDR4 will fail initialization.

failure_modes.0V: LDO/Buck 4 failure or sequencing issue. Check if VDD_DDR came up first.
failure_modes.Present but DDR fails: Sequencing problem — VPP may be coming up before VDD_DDR.

TP503.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 2 (1.8V/2A, 1MHz) → TP503 → Waikiki QCN9274 VDDA + Napa QCA8081 VDD_IO
TP503.description: CRITICAL SHARED RAIL. 1.8V supply shared between Waikiki WiFi analog (QCN9274 VDDA) and Napa Ethernet PHY I/O (QCA8081 VDD_IO). This is a SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE — if this rail dies, BOTH WiFi AND Ethernet are dead simultaneously.

failure_modes.0V: Buck 2 failure. Check SPBM enable signal. This kills WiFi AND Ethernet.
failure_modes.<1.7V: Overloaded — one of the loads may have a short. Disconnect Waikiki/Napa to isolate.
failure_modes.WiFi+Ethernet both dead: Almost certainly this rail. Check TP503 first.

TP28.schematic_path: 1.8V or 3.3V → LDO → TP28 → Miami analog reference pins
TP28.description: 0.8V analog reference voltage. Used by Miami's internal ADCs and analog circuits. Generated by a dedicated LDO from the 1.8V or 3.3V rail.

failure_modes.0V: LDO failure. Check enable pin and input supply voltage.

TP36.schematic_path: 1.8V or 3.3V → LDO → TP36 → Miami PLL analog pins
TP36.description: 1.2V analog supply for Miami's PLL (Phase-Locked Loop) circuits. Used for clock generation and frequency synthesis. MONITOR ONLY — out-of-spec may cause PLL jitter or clock drift but does not indicate board-level failure on its own.

failure_modes.Out of spec: May cause clock jitter. Monitor only — not a board failure indicator.

TP504.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 5 (1.05V/2A, 1MHz) → TP504 → Napa QCA8081 VDD_CORE pins
TP504.description: 1.05V digital core supply for Napa QCA8081 2.5GBASE-T Ethernet PHY. Needs BOTH this rail AND the 1.8V shared rail (TP503) to function. If 1.05V is present but 1.8V is dead, Ethernet still won't work.

failure_modes.0V: Buck 5 failure. Check enable from SPBM.
failure_modes.Present but no Ethernet: Check TP503 (1.8V shared). Also check RJ45 connector (bent pins, corrosion), magnetics continuity (<2Ω per winding), SGMII/MDIO signals.

TP573.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 6 (3.3V/3A, 700KHz) → TP573 → Waikiki QCN9274 DVDD pins
TP573.description: 3.3V main digital supply for Waikiki QCN9274 WiFi 7 radio. Powers digital I/O and PCIe interface. If present but no WiFi, the issue is likely PCIe link (check PERST_N signal, 100MHz reference clock).

failure_modes.Present but no WiFi: PCIe link issue. Check PERST_N (should go HIGH after power stable). Scope 100MHz PCIe reference clock. Via UART: lspci should show QCN9274.

TP535.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Distribution → TP535 → Waikiki QCN9274 5V input
TP535.description: 5V supply to the Waikiki WiFi subsystem. Distributed from the main 5V bus. If missing, the entire Waikiki subsystem loses its primary power input.

failure_modes.0V: 5V bus distribution issue. Check main 5V at TP1205 first. Then check ferrite bead/fuse to Waikiki.
failure_modes.<4.75V: Excess load or cap degradation on Waikiki 5V input.

TP589.description: Filtered version of the 3.3V Waikiki supply. Should track TP573 closely. A significant difference indicates an isolation component (ferrite bead, fuse, or filter cap) has failed.
key_components: Ferrite bead or filter between TP573 and TP589

failure_modes.Differs from TP573: Isolation component open or shorted. Check ferrite bead continuity.
failure_modes.Both 0V: Upstream Buck 6 failure — debug at TP573.

TP34.schematic_path: LDO → TP34 → Miami/Waikiki PCIe SerDes analog pins
TP34.description: 0.925V analog supply for PCIe SerDes (Serializer/Deserializer). Powers the high-speed analog circuits in the PCIe link between Miami and Waikiki. MONITOR ONLY — WiFi failure is more likely caused by DVDD3.3 or PERST_N issues.

failure_modes.Out of spec: May degrade PCIe link margin. Monitor only — check DVDD3.3 and PERST_N first for WiFi issues.

TP30.schematic_path: LDO → TP30 → Miami/Waikiki PCIe I/O level shifters
TP30.description: 1.8V supply for PCIe I/O interface between Miami and Waikiki. Required for the digital signaling layer of the PCIe link. Without this, Miami and Waikiki cannot communicate even if both are powered.

failure_modes.0V: PCIe I/O LDO failure. No Miami-Waikiki communication possible.

TP31.description: Additional 1.8V domain for PX3 interface. Separate from the shared 1.8V rail (TP503). If this is missing while other 1.8V rails are OK, it's a local LDO issue.

failure_modes.0V while other 1.8V OK: Local PX3 LDO failure. Check enable and input.

TP569.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 8 (4.2V/2A, 500KHz) → TP569 → SKY85500-11 FEM x2 VCC pins
TP569.description: HIGHEST VOLTAGE RAIL on the board. 4.2V supply for two SKY85500-11 5GHz Front End Modules (FEMs). Peak power draw is 8.4W (4.2V × 2A). Each FEM draws ~300mA during TX. If a PA is shorted, this rail will be pulled low.

failure_modes.<4.0V: FEM excess current — one PA may be shorted. Measure current at each FEM VCC (~300mA during TX). 0mA = PA open (burned out).
failure_modes.Present but no 5G: FEM or SAW/BPF filter issue. Check diplexer path. Compare TX power to KGU (>3dB below = degradation).

TP577.schematic_path: 5V Bus → Buck 7 (3.3V/2A, 700KHz) → TP577 → Miami IPQ5332 internal 2.4G PA
TP577.description: 3.3V supply for Miami's internal 2.4GHz power amplifier (IPA). Unlike 5GHz which uses external FEMs, the 2.4GHz PA is integrated inside the Miami SoC. If this rail is present but 2.4G is dead, the issue is the IPA circuit or SAW filters.

failure_modes.Present but no 2.4G: Miami internal PA damaged or SAW filter failure. SAW filters may vary between batches. Check diplexer path.

TP55.schematic_path: PoE Input → Standby LDO → TP55 → Always-on peripherals
TP55.description: 3.3V standby rail that is always present whenever PoE power is connected, even before the SPBM starts the main power sequence. If this is missing, it indicates a very early power failure in the input stage.

failure_modes.0V: Very early power failure. PoE input may be present but standby LDO is dead. Check input to LDO.

TP590.schematic_path: 3.3V Bus → TP590 → KTD2027B LED Driver → RGB LED
TP590.description: 3.3V supply for the KTD2027B I2C-controlled RGB LED driver. If this rail is present but the LED is dark, the issue is the I2C bus communication or the KTD2027B IC itself.

failure_modes.0V: No LED at all. 3.3V bus distribution issue.
failure_modes.Present but LED dark: I2C bus failure or KTD2027B IC dead. Check I2C pull-ups and bus signals.

TP56.schematic_path: USB-C Connector CC pins → FUSB15201MX → TP56 → Miami GPIO
TP56.description: USB-C CC (Configuration Channel) pin voltage indicating cable orientation. The FUSB15201MX detects which way the USB-C cable is inserted and routes signals accordingly. MONITOR ONLY — does not affect core board function. Used for debug UART access via USB-C SBU pins.

failure_modes.Out of spec: CC resistor network issue. Monitor only — does not affect core board function.

PoE Input.title: PoE Input Stage Fault Isolation
steps: 1. Measure PoE input at cable center taps (pins 4,5=V+; 7,8=V-)
2. If 0V: Check cable continuity, PoE injector output, magnetics
3. If 42.5-57V present: Check MPM3690 ENABLE pin (should be HIGH)
4. Measure 5V output at TP1205. If 0V, MPM3690 not switching
5. Check classification resistor (~24.9K for Class 4 / 802.3at)
6. Scope 5V rail for ripple: >50mV pk-pk = cap degradation
7. Check TMP709 thermal switch (TP1211): if LOW, thermal shutdown

Miami SoC Core.title: Miami SoC Core Fault Isolation
steps: 1. Verify 5V rail OK (Phase 1) before debugging Miami rails
2. Check SPBM (SLG4R44724TR) enable output for 0.9V buck
3. If TP579 VDD_CX=0V: Measure resistance VCC_CX to GND (>5ohm OK)
4. If <1ohm: Miami die short. If >5ohm: Buck 1 converter failure
5. Check TP27 vs TP579: should be close. Delta=series filter issue
6. Check TP29 VDD_SOC_MX: separate domain, own regulator
7. Check TP578 PMU 1.95V: needed for Miami internal LDOs
8. Connect UART (USB-C SBU pins, 115200 baud): any output=alive

DDR4 Memory.title: DDR4 Memory Fault Isolation
steps: 1. Check TP574 VDD_DDR first: DDR4 core power
2. Check TP576 VPP: must come up AFTER VDD_DDR is stable
3. If both present: connect UART, look for DDR training messages
4. DDR training failed: Scope VDD_DDR ripple (AC coupled, 20MHz BW)
5. Ripple >30mV: Output cap degradation on 1.2V rail
6. Ripple OK: DDR4 BGA solder joint suspect (RPN=162, #3 risk)
7. X-ray DDR4 BGA if available: look for cracked balls
8. Thermal cycle test: heat 55C / cool 0C, monitor boot

Shared / Analog.title: Shared 1.8V Rail Fault Isolation
steps: 1. TP503 should read ~1.8V
2. If dead: Buck 2 failure. Check enable from SPBM.
3. WARNING: This rail feeds Waikiki analog AND Napa PHY I/O
4. If 1.8V dead: expect BOTH WiFi and Ethernet non-functional
5. Check TP28 (0.8V) and TP36 (1.2V): separate analog LDOs
6. If 0.8V or 1.2V missing: respective LDO failed
7. Check enable pins and input supply for failed LDO

Ethernet PHY (Napa).title: Ethernet PHY Fault Isolation
steps: 1. Verify TP504 (1.05V core) AND TP503 (1.8V I/O) both present
2. If 1.05V missing: Buck 5 failure
3. Both present but no Ethernet: check RJ45 (bent pins, corrosion)
4. Check magnetics continuity (<2ohm per winding)
5. Via UART: ethtool eth0 -> check link status and speed
6. Link: no -> Check MDI signals with scope at Napa pins
7. Link up but no data: Check SGMII between Miami and Napa
8. Speed stuck at 100M: Cable issue (only 2 pairs working)

WiFi (Waikiki).title: WiFi / Waikiki / PCIe Fault Isolation
steps: 1. Check TP573 DVDD3.3 first: Waikiki main digital supply
2. Check TP535 DVDD5: 5V to Waikiki subsystem
3. Check PCIe rails: TP34 (0.925V SerDes) and TP30 (1.8V I/O)
4. All present: Via UART lspci should show QCN9274
5. Not listed: Check PERST_N signal (should go HIGH after power)
6. Scope PCIe reference clock (100MHz differential)
7. PCIe link up but no WiFi: Driver issue or Waikiki firmware
8. Check TP31 VDD_1V8_PX3: additional 1.8V domain

RF Power Amps.title: RF Power Amplifier Fault Isolation
steps: 1. Check TP569 VDD_XPA (4.2V): 5GHz FEM supply (HIGHEST RAIL)
2. If 0V: Buck 8 failure. If <4.0V: FEM excess current (PA short)
3. Check TP577 AVDD3.3_2G: 2.4GHz internal PA supply
4. 5G dead: Measure current at each FEM VCC (~300mA during TX)
5. 0mA during TX: PA open (burned out). Replace SKY85500-11.
6. 2.4G dead: Check SAW filters (part may vary between batches)
7. Check diplexer paths with network analyzer if available
8. Compare TX power to KGU: >3dB below=component degradation

Standby / Misc.title: Standby / Misc Fault Isolation
steps: 1. TP55 STBY_VDD3.3 should be present whenever PoE connected
2. If missing: Very early power failure, before SPBM starts
3. TP590 LED supply: if 0V, no LED (unit may work but dark)
4. Check I2C bus to KTD2027B if LED supply present but LED off
5. TP56 USB-C orientation: depends on cable, for debug port
6. POE_POWER_QSDK: total system power at full OS, 3-12.9W
7. If >12.9W: abnormal draw, thermal camera for shorted component
